intro: Above the shore, in Antalya province, lies Beldibi Cave, whose story reaches back to 15,000 BC. Human and animal figures are incised on the walls of this rock shelter, among the oldest rock art known in Anatolia.
history: This rock shelter above the shore was excavated by Enver Bostancı in the 1950s. The human and animal figures incised on its walls were made by a community living through a great change: the passage from the end of the ice age into the Neolithic. They are among the oldest rock art known in Anatolia.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the rock art, the incised figures, the Epipalaeolithic layers and the shell finds.
facts: Did you know? The sea shells found in the shelter show that the community here drew regularly on the resources of the coast. And the figures incised on the shelter walls are among the oldest rock art known in Anatolia.
outro: This brings our tour of Beldibi Cave to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
